chunks: And with this chain of narrators, he said: I heard him say:

When a believer stands up for prayer, Allah sends forth the Hur al-Ayn (heavenly maidens) until they surround him. If he finishes [the prayer] and does not ask Allah for any of them, they depart while being astonished.

key_terms.الْحُورَ الْعَيْنَ: Hur al-Ayn, heavenly maidens of Paradise

ai.seo_question: What happens to the heavenly maidens when a believer finishes his prayer without asking for them?
ai.summary: In Fadail al-Shia, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates that the Hur al-Ayn are dispatched to gaze upon the praying believer, reflecting the cosmic significance of Salah in Shia tradition. If the believer neglects to ask Allah for their companionship, they depart in astonishment, highlighting the believer's potential to attain higher spiritual ranks through specific supplications.

en.badr-shahin: (The same previous series of relaters)… that Abu Abdullah (a) said:

When a believer stands up for offering a prayer, Allah allows the women of Paradise to look at him. If he finishes his prayer without asking Allah to give him women of Paradise in marriage, they go back with astonishment.
